records.title: NOTIF_CONFIG_DATA(39) stripped on PCI-modern despite validator + notify-data path
records.reachability_analysis: no guard; defect path reached unconditionally. vring_transport_features (virtio_ring.c:3505-3532) has no case label for VIRTIO_F_NOTIF_CONFIG_DATA(39); every finalize hits default at 3527-3529 and clears bit 39. vp_transport_features (367-381) re-adds SR_IOV/RING_RESET/ADMIN_VQ but not bit 39 (full-body search). So after vp_finalize_features the bit is always 0 on modern PCI even though vp_check_common_size (:407) validated the common-cfg queue_notify_data field. Mechanical receipt vring_transport_features_cases.txt confirms 8 case labels, bit 39 absent.

records.title: vp_interrupt returns IRQ_NONE for a config-change-only interrupt
records.reachability_analysis: no guard; defect path reached unconditionally. In vp_interrupt (virtio_pci_common.c:111-124) isr is non-zero for a config interrupt (VIRTIO_PCI_ISR_CONFIG=0x2), so the `if (!isr) return IRQ_NONE` at :116-117 is not taken. At :120-121 vp_config_changed's IRQ_HANDLED return is discarded; the function returns vp_vring_interrupt (:123), which is IRQ_NONE when no vq is serviced. For a config-only interrupt with no concurrent vring activity vp_interrupt reports IRQ_NONE. Reachable on shared-vector (single MSI-X / INTx) configs; no upstream guard.

records.title: vm_reset omits the spec section 5 wait-for-status-zero poll
records.reachability_analysis: no guard; defect path reached unconditionally. vm_reset (virtio_mmio.c:251-257) writes 0 to VIRTIO_MMIO_STATUS and returns immediately -- two statements, no readback loop. The reset contract is satisfied inside each transport's .reset op (vp_reset and vp_legacy implement the readback); there is no caller-side compensating poll. So spec section 5 (write 0, then read device_status until 0) is unmet for every MMIO reset.
